newsitem.title: ITALY: Vranitzky sees no alternative to military force.
newsitem.headline: Vranitzky sees no alternative to military force.

text.p: European envoy Franz Vranitzky said on Friday that he saw no alternative to outside military intervention to halt the anarchy and chaos spreading through Albania.

"I will report that there is no alternative as far as I can see," Vranitzky told reporters after separate talks with the Albanian government and rebel representatives. "The decision has to be taken very quickly," he said.

Vranitzky, the former Austrian chancellor, was speaking in the southern Italian port of Brindisi after meeting the parties on an Italian warship in the Adriatic as part of his mission for the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE).

He acknowledged that the 54-member OSCE, which comprises European countries and the United States and Canada, was not unanimously behind military action but said he hoped that individual members could volunteer for any force.

"I am afraid we won't get all 54. The idea has arisen of (creating) a coalition of the willing. That means the decision- making could be shortened with regard to the established institutions," Vranitzky said.

He said rebels he had met had expressed confidence in Albania's new national unity government but apprehension over President Sali Berisha. Insurgents who have seized most of southern Albania are demanding Berisha's resignation.
